rationale: Start with a broad gradient at intermediate temperature to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing retained compounds. This provides a baseline for narrowing the solvent window and testing slope and temperature selectivity.

Halve the gradient duration to reduce the time penalty while testing how the closest pairs respond to increased slope. The initial run has substantial resolution margin and all compounds elute well within the gradient.

Test temperature selectivity at the fast gradient, targeting the crowded middle cluster without adding gradient time. Higher temperature should also shorten retention, preserving the zero time penalty.

Moderately lengthen the fast gradient to recover resolution in the middle cluster while keeping the last peak near eight minutes. The two 40 C runs show that the critical pair responds strongly to gradient duration.
Test just below 60 C to move away from its near-coeluting pair while retaining temperature-driven separation in the middle cluster. The short gradient should maintain a zero time penalty.

Slightly flatten the best-performing gradient to improve its remaining under-resolved pair. This also tests whether the neighboring pair retains adequate separation, with enough time margin to keep the time penalty at zero.

Injection 6 already achieves the maximum CRF and remains the benchmark. Slightly reduce the gradient slope to test a nearby optimum, aiming to improve the 1.59-resolution pair while preserving the other critical pair and zero time penalty.

The maximum CRF is already secured; this tests an alternative with potentially more balanced critical-pair resolution. A shallower gradient may resolve the pair that overlapped at 60 C, while higher temperature limits the added retention time.

Test a slightly higher starting organic fraction around the maximum-scoring method to shorten retention and probe critical-pair selectivity. The first peak was sufficiently retained to justify this modest increase; injection 6 remains the benchmark.

Slightly reduce the slope from injection 9 to improve its R=1.29 pair while retaining the other critical pair's resolution margin. This may recover maximum CRF with a higher starting organic fraction and no time penalty.

Reduce the slope one more grid step to bring the R=1.47 pair above 1.5 while preserving the neighboring pair's margin. The last peak should remain within the gradient and the zero-time-penalty region.

With maximum CRF secured, test a narrower solvent window for greater critical-pair resolution margin. The higher start may improve the temperature-sensitive pair, while the shallower slope should compensate for compression of the earlier pair without exceeding the time allowance.

Refine the maximum-scoring method from injection 11 with a slightly shallower gradient. This should increase separation of its earlier critical pair while keeping the later pair above 1.5 and the last peak within the zero-time-penalty region.

Maximum CRF is already secured, so test a cooler selectivity regime for an alternative fast method. Cooling may separate the middle pair that nearly coeluted at 40 C, while the steep gradient limits the increase in last-peak retention.

Test modest cooling from injection 4 to shift its critical middle pair away from overlap without the extensive crowding seen at 25 C. This may identify another maximum-scoring temperature regime while keeping last-peak retention near the zero-penalty window.

Return to the maximum-scoring 55 C region and test a slope between those of injections 11 and 13. This should retain full resolution and zero time penalty while providing a higher final organic fraction for column washing.

The maximum CRF is already secured; test whether 50 C offers a faster fully resolved alternative. Relative to injection 5, modest cooling should improve its earlier critical pair, while revealing whether the later pair retains sufficient separation.

Use a slightly shallower slope than injection 12 to lift its R=1.41 pair above baseline resolution while preserving the other critical pair's margin. The last peak is expected near nine minutes, testing the edge of the zero-time-penalty region; existing maximum-scoring methods remain the benchmarks.

Test a shorter programmed gradient with nearly the same slope as maximum-scoring injection 16. The final organic fraction remains above the estimated last-peak elution fraction, so this should preserve full resolution and zero time penalty while reaching the final hold sooner.

Slightly steepen injection 19 to shorten retention and balance the two critical-pair resolutions. Interpolation between injections 10 and 11 suggests both should remain above 1.5, preserving maximum CRF.

Trim the maximum-scoring injection 6 to the same initial fraction and gradient slope but an earlier endpoint. The last peak should still elute before the gradient ends at the outlet, preserving maximum CRF with a shorter programmed gradient.

Trim injection 11 to an eight-minute gradient while preserving its starting fraction and slope, which gave a minimum resolution of 1.58. The last peak should elute before the gradient ends at the outlet, retaining maximum CRF with a shorter programmed gradient.

Keep the successful slope of injection 21 but end the gradient after the first nine peaks, allowing the isolated last compound to elute during the hold. This tests whether a shorter programmed gradient and lower final organic fraction can retain maximum CRF without delaying the last peak beyond nine minutes.

Test a slightly shallower, lower-endpoint variant of injection 22 to increase the earlier critical pair's resolution while preserving the later pair. The last peak may enter the final hold, but is expected to remain near the zero-time-penalty window; maximum CRF is already secured.

Finish with an untested method preserving the starting fraction, temperature, and slope of maximum-scoring injection 6 while shortening the programmed gradient. All peaks should remain within the gradient, reproducing full resolution and zero time penalty; the campaign has already reached the maximum possible CRF.
